title: Find Subarray With Bitwise OR Closest to K
statement: Choose any subarray `nums[l..r]` of `nums` (a contiguous, non-empty run of elements) and combine its elements with bitwise OR. Return the smallest value of `|k - OR|` that any choice of subarray can give.
notes:
## Intuition

Checking every subarray while growing its OR is O(n²), too slow for 10^5 numbers. But OR only ever turns bits on: fix a right end and extend the subarray to the left, and the OR either stays the same or gains a new bit. Values fit in 30 bits, so all subarrays ending at one index share at most 30 **distinct** OR values. Keeping just those values for the current right end is enough to try every OR that any subarray can have.

## Approach

1. Keep `ors`: the distinct OR values of subarrays ending at the previous index, ordered from the shortest subarray to the longest.
2. For each `num`, start `next` with `[num]` (the subarray of length one).
3. Extend every previous subarray by `num`: `merged = value | num`. These come out non-decreasing, so a duplicate can only equal the last entry of `next`; skip it in that case.
4. Every value in `next` is the OR of some subarray, so update `best` with `Math.abs(k - value)`.
5. Replace `ors` with `next` and continue. Return `best`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [1, 2, 4, 5]`, `k = 3`.

- `num = 1`: `next = [1]`, `best = |3 - 1| = 2`.
- `num = 2`: `next = [2, 3]` (`1 | 2 = 3`). `|3 - 3| = 0`, so `best = 0`.
- `num = 4`: `next = [4, 6, 7]`; nothing beats 0.
- `num = 5`: `next = [5, 7]` (`4 | 5 = 5` repeats and is skipped, `6 | 5 = 7`, `7 | 5 = 7` repeats). The answer is `0`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n · B) with B = 30 bits, because `ors` never holds more than B distinct values.
- Space: O(B) for the two short lists.

## Pitfalls

- Storing every subarray's OR instead of only the distinct ones brings back O(n²) work.
- Removing duplicates by comparing with the last entry only works because the values are kept in non-decreasing order; do not shuffle them.
- The OR can be larger than `k` as well as smaller, so take the absolute difference rather than `k - value`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `best` | smallest difference found so far |
| `ors` | distinct OR values of subarrays ending at the previous index |
| `num` | the current element, the new right end |
| `next` | distinct OR values of subarrays ending at `num` |
| `merged` | an older subarray's OR extended by `num` |
| `value` | one OR value being extended or scored |
